transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… lately I’ve been noticing my eating gets kind of out of hand. Like after a really long day on site, or sometimes after one of those neighborhood meetings that somehow goes on forever, I’ll get home and just start eating whatever’s there—leftover takeout, cereal, chips, just random stuff—and it ends up being way more than I meant to eat. Then I’m sitting there uncomfortably full and feeling pretty bad about it.
Do you feel guilty after these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it guilt exactly. I feel pretty lousy afterward, like annoyed with myself, but then I’ll start thinking about what I should’ve made for dinner instead, or whether I even bought groceries—because my schedule gets so weird with job sites moving around. So… yeah, I’m not totally sure how to answer that.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during those times?

Yeah… I think that’s the part that scares me a little. Once I start on those evenings, it kind of feels like I’m on autopilot. Like I’ll be standing there thinking, “Okay, stop, you’ve got an early crew start tomorrow,” and then somehow I’m back in the kitchen getting more. It’s not like I’m enjoying it that much by then, it just keeps going.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during those times?

Not really, no. I mean, at the start I’ll think I’m just having something quick, and then it’s like I’m on autopilot. I’ll even be telling myself, “You need to stop, you’ve got an early crew start tomorrow,” and then somehow I’m back in the kitchen getting more. It feels kind of embarrassing to say, but in those moments it doesn’t really feel like I’m choosing anymore.
Do you remember everything that happens while you're eating during those episodes?

Um… I think so? I mean, it’s not like I black out or anything, if that’s what you mean. I can usually remember being in the kitchen, what I grabbed, that kind of thing.

But honestly sometimes it all kind of blends together, especially if I’m tired after work. Like, I’ll remember I ate, but then I’m thinking about whether I locked up the site trailer or if the guys have the right materials for the morning, and it’s hard to separate what happened when. So… I don’t think I’m missing time, exactly.
Are you aware of how much you're eating while it's happening during those episodes?

Sort of… I mean, I’m aware enough to know it’s more than I meant to have, if that makes sense. But once I start on those evenings, it feels like I’m on autopilot. I’ll be thinking, “Stop, you’ve got an early crew start,” and then I’m still walking back into the kitchen for more.

And then my mind jumps to stupid work stuff, like whether I told someone to move the forms or if we’re short on material, and I’m eating while half-thinking about that. So I’m aware, but not really keeping track or feeling in control of it.
Do you ever feel self-criticism or criticize yourself after these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I’ll start thinking I’m ridiculous for letting it happen again, and then it kind of turns into checking how I look, if that makes sense.

Like, since I started wearing more fitted work clothes and having to be up front in meetings more, I’ll judge the whole day by whether my pants feel tight or whether I think people can see my stomach. Which is stupid, because half the guys are probably thinking about concrete deliveries or whatever, not me, but I still get stuck on it. After I eat more than I meant to, that voice is definitely worse.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. It’s not like I’m sitting there doing math about pounds, exactly, but I do get really stuck on whether I look bigger.

Since I started wearing more fitted work clothes and having to be up front in meetings, I catch myself judging the whole day by whether my pants feel tight, or whether I think people can see my stomach. And then I’ll be trying to listen to someone talk about a schedule change or materials or whatever, and part of my brain is just on that. So… yeah, I guess I am afraid of it.
Does worrying about your weight affect your daily activities or how you interact with others?

Yeah, a bit. I mean, I’m still going to work, I’m still getting things done, people aren’t like… pulling me aside or anything. But I have started avoiding some stuff after meetings, like if everyone’s going to grab food or someone says, “Let’s go eat,” I’ll make an excuse.

Sometimes I just rush home instead, because I’m worried if I stay out or if the evening gets too loose, I’ll kind of lose the handle on it. And then I’ll spend the whole time thinking about that instead of just talking like a normal person. So it’s not ruining everything, but it is changing what I say yes to.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Yeah… sometimes. Not every time, but a few times a month after those nights, I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s embarrassing to say out loud. It’s usually when I panic and feel like I’ve just undone all this effort to look… put-together, I guess. Like I’ve spent the whole week trying to seem professional and in control, and then after eating too much it feels like I’ve wrecked it. So I tell myself I just need to “fix” it, even though I know that sounds bad.
How often do these episodes of eating more than you meant to happen?

Um… if I’m being honest, looking back over the last few months, it’s probably averaged out to about once a week.

It’s not like every Tuesday or anything neat like that. Some weeks it might happen twice, especially if work is stressful or there are meals with people, and then another week maybe not at all. I kind of lose track because I tell myself it was “just that one night,” but when I add it up… yeah, around weekly.
Do you ever exercise more than usual after one of these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Um… I don’t know that I’d say I exercise more after, not in any planned way. Like I’m not going, “Okay, now I have to do an extra workout,” exactly.

I mean, sometimes I’ll feel restless and tell myself I should move around, but honestly my schedule is all over the place with work anyway, and some days I’m already walking around sites or climbing stairs and by the time I get home I’m just… done. So I haven’t really noticed a pattern like that after those nights.
Do you usually make yourself vomit after these episodes of eating more than you meant to, or are there other ways you try to compensate?

Mostly it’s the throwing up, yeah… not usually, like every single time, but a few times a month after those nights I’ll end up in the bathroom making myself vomit.

I don’t really have some whole routine, if that makes sense. It’s more like I panic. I start thinking I’ve ruined everything, like all the effort I put into looking put-together at work and seeming like I have it handled. Which is stupid because nobody’s probably thinking about it as much as I am, but in the moment it feels like I have to undo it somehow.
How often do you make yourself vomit after eating more than you meant to?

A few times a month, I think. Not every time it happens, but after some of those nights I’ll end up going into the bathroom and making myself throw up.

It’s usually when I kind of panic, like I’ve messed up all the work I put into keeping myself looking put-together. Which sounds shallow when I say it out loud, especially with my job where I’m supposed to be the one in control and organized, but… yeah. A few times a month.
Do you make yourself vomit after every episode of eating more than you meant to, or is it less often?

No, not every time. It’s more like… a few times a month, after certain nights when I really panic. I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up because I get this feeling like I need to undo it, like I’ve messed up all the work I put into looking put-together.

And I know that probably sounds kind of ridiculous, because half the time I’m worrying about how I look at work or whether people think I have everything handled, when really they’re probably thinking about permits or schedules or whatever. But, yeah… it’s less often than every episode. A few times a month.
Does making yourself vomit happen after most episodes of eating more than you meant to, or is it more occasional?

It’s more occasional. I mean, it’s not after most of them. It’s a few times a month, usually after those nights where I really freak out and feel like I need to undo it somehow.

I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up, and it’s… I don’t know, it’s tied up with this panic about looking like I have everything together. Which is kind of embarrassing to say, because at work I’m around crews and schedules and everyone expects me to be organized, and then I’m at home doing this. But yeah, more occasional. A few times a month.
Does making yourself vomit usually happen on the same day as the episode of eating more than you meant to?

Yeah, usually it’s that same night. Like if I’ve had one of those nights where I ate more than I meant to and then I start panicking, I’ll go into the bathroom pretty soon after and make myself throw up.

It’s not like I plan it for later or anything. It’s more this immediate “I need to undo this” feeling, which… I know sounds intense. And then I start thinking about work and how I’m supposed to look like I have everything handled, like if I can manage crews and schedules then I should be able to manage myself, which is probably not really the point of your question. But yes, it’s usually the same day, a few times a month after those nights.
Does making yourself vomit happen after almost every episode of eating more than you meant to, or is it less frequent than that?

No, it’s definitely less frequent than that. Not after almost every time. It’s more like… a few times a month, after those nights when I really spiral about it.

I’ll end up going into the bathroom and making myself throw up because I feel like I need to undo it, like I’ve ruined all this effort I put into looking put-together. Which is silly, I guess, because nobody on a job site is standing there analyzing me the way I think they are, they’re worried about their own stuff… but in the moment it feels really urgent. So, yeah, a few times a month, not every episode.
Do you make yourself vomit at least once a week?

If I average it out, yeah… I think it comes out to about once a week over the last few months. It doesn’t happen neatly every week, though. Like, some weeks it might happen twice if I’m really off, and then another week not at all.

I’m bad at tracking it because my schedule gets weird with work, and then I’ll tell myself, “Oh, it hasn’t been that often,” but looking back, the whole overeating and then making myself throw up pattern is probably around weekly.
Do you make yourself vomit at least once a week for at least three months?

Yeah… I think so. Looking back over the last few months, it’s averaged out to about once a week, even if it doesn’t happen in this neat, predictable way.

Like some weeks it’s twice, and then I’ll have a week where it doesn’t happen at all, and I’ll use that to tell myself it’s not really a pattern. I do that with work stuff too, like if one project goes smoothly I pretend the whole month wasn’t chaos. But… if I’m being honest, the overeating and then making myself throw up has been going on about weekly for at least the last few months.

doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit at least once a week?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Looking back over the last few months, the overeating-and-then-purging pattern has averaged about weekly, even if some weeks it happens twice and other weeks not at all.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether self-induced vomiting occurs at least once a week, which directly relates to the frequency criterion for compensatory behaviors.

patient.answer:
If I average it out, yeah… I think it comes out to about once a week over the last few months. It doesn’t happen neatly every week, though. Like, some weeks it might happen twice if I’m really off, and then another week not at all.

I’m bad at tracking it because my schedule gets weird with work, and then I’ll tell myself, “Oh, it hasn’t been that often,” but looking back, the whole overeating and then making myself throw up pattern is probably around weekly.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's behavior meets the frequency criteria for bulimia nervosa
doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit at least once a week for at least three months?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Looking back over the last few months, the overeating-and-then-purging pattern has averaged about weekly, even if some weeks it happens twice and other weeks not at all.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the vomiting occurs at least weekly for at least three months, which directly matches the frequency and duration requirement for binge eating and compensatory behaviors.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. Looking back over the last few months, it’s averaged out to about once a week, even if it doesn’t happen in this neat, predictable way.

Like some weeks it’s twice, and then I’ll have a week where it doesn’t happen at all, and I’ll use that to tell myself it’s not really a pattern. I do that with work stuff too, like if one project goes smoothly I pretend the whole month wasn’t chaos. But… if I’m being honest, the overeating and then making myself throw up has been going on about weekly for at least the last few months.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of recurrent episodes of eating more than intended, lack of control during these episodes, and subsequent purging behavior through self-induced vomiting at least once a week for at least three months meet the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa.
